items.title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said he is optimistic that Tetairoa McMillan (foot) will play in Week 12 against the Bucs.
items.text: McMillan limped off the field in Week 11 with the foot issue but eventually returned to and finished the game. He did not practice today, though it’s not officially a DNP. The Panthers’ first practice of the week is tomorrow since they play on Monday, which will give McMillan an extra day to recover. Assuming all goes well in practice this week, McMillan will remain a fantasy WR2 for a must-win matchup with the Bucs. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said that Derrick Henry “had a couple of small symptoms” and is now in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
items.text: Minter adds that he expects Henry to play in Week 12 against the Texans. On Sunday, it was reported that Henry had cleared the concussion protocol after the Ravens’ Week 11 loss to the Panthers. Re-entering the concussion protocol mid-week seems like a bad sign. Justice Hill has played well in recent weeks and would presumably start in Henry’s stead if the burly back is unable to play. Hill is backed up by Rasheen Ali and rookie Adam Randall, the latter of whom could be worth adding in deep leagues. Henry was limited at practice today. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac reports the Steelers are expected to release Aaron Rodgers.
items.text: The team announced his benching late Tuesday night. He then went on The Pat McAfee Show earlier today and burned every bridge in town by saying Mike McCarthy has been sleeping through meetings or missing them outright, among many other accusations. Per Dulac, the interview hastened Pittsburgh’s decision to get Rodgers off the roster. Once he clears waivers, Rodgers will be eligible to sign with another team. items.title: Mike Evans (Achilles) did not practice on Wednesday.
items.text: This is almost certainly just load management for the superstar wide receiver. Evans returned ot action last week, posting a 6/109/1 receiving line. He should be viewed as a talent- and volume-based WR2 against the Seahawks’ top-tier defense. Jordan Watkins (groin) will also sit out on Wednesday. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Bears ruled out Roschon Johnson (ankle) for Week 12 against the Lions.
items.text: Johnson will be replaced by Salvon Ahmed as the Bears’ No. 3 running back. Ahmed does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, with D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai splitting reps. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Bears ruled out Kyler Gordon (shoulder) for Week 12 against the Lions.
items.text: Bears No. 2 perimeter CB Tyrique Stevenson (groin) is questionable to play, which could mean that the Bears are without two of their top-three cornerbacks against the Lions’ elite offense. Tomorrow’s NFC North is looking like a fantasy-friendly environment. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Brock Purdy (ankle) will not practice Wednesday.
items.text: Purdy sprained his ankle in the second quarter of his Week 11 win over the Vikings. He played through the issue but, according to Kyle Shanahan, is now considered day-to-day. With a NFC West bout versus Seattle on tap, we suspect Purdy will play in Week 12 despite the injury. On the other hand, Mac Jones was extremely successful under center last year, so the 49ers wouldn’t be in a terrible spot if they are forced to sit Purdy for a week. Between the injury and the nightmare matchup, Purdy will shuffle to the back of the QB1 ranks this week. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: 49ers placed RT Colton McKivitz on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
items.text: This is extremely unfortunate. The 49ers’ talented right tackle is expected to miss the rest of the season after fracturing and dislocating his ankle. The 49ers remain an elite team, but McKivitz’s loss will likely be felt on the field from time to time. The 49ers also activated CB Nate Hobbs from injured reserve and re-signed WR Brandin Cooks to the practice squad. - Nic Bodiford

items.title: Jake Ferguson (ankle/knee) will not play in Week 12 against the Eagles.
items.text: Ferguson failed to practice at any point this week and will miss his second straight game. Brevyn Spann-Ford will be the next man up versus Philly. He caught both of his targets for five yards and a touchdown last week. “BSF” will be a touchdown-or-bust TE2 for Week 12. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, Aaron Rodgers said he issued an ultimatum to Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy to give up play-calling duties.
items.text: Rodgers started off the conversation talking about McCarthy’s shortcomings this year, but he quickly shifted toward accusing McCarthy of being “unwell.” He mentioned several instances of McCarthy missing meetings while sleeping in his office or falling asleep during others. Rodgers also talked extensively about McCarthy failing to stay ahead on film sessions and even brought up a moment on the sidelines when McCarthy broke the huddle with a “1, 2, 3, Packers”.
